The compaction request itself is clear, though, and the book is in the conversation. Here are the notes.

# NOTES: *Lord Stranleigh Abroad* by Robert Barr (Ward, Locke & Co., 1913)

Front matter: Gutenberg #32185. Frontispiece: "'Why did you wish to murder me?'" (p.189). Chapters: I Lord Stranleigh All at Sea (p.7); II An Automobile Ride (49); III The God in the Car (87); IV The Mad Miss Maturin (125); V In Search of Game (164); VI The Bunk House Prisoner (209); VII The End of the Contest (259). Single book, no sub-books. Back matter is Ward, Lock publisher's ads (ignore).

## Ch. I: Lord Stranleigh All at Sea
- Edmund Trevelyan (= Lord Evelyn Trevelyan / Stranleigh, Wychwood) boards liner at Southampton, noon, hot summer day. Route: Cherbourg, Queenstown, New York. Largest Atlantic liner.
- Valet Ponderby: dislikes ocean travel, America; disdains equality.
- Doctor (ship's medical officer, promoted; "most skilful and most popular medical officer on the Atlantic"); seats Trevelyan at right-hand table. Doctor unnamed.
- Hon. John Hazel: ex-club member, cardsharp, expelled from Camperdown Club after being found out; was Stranleigh's frequent victim; forgiven repeatedly. Plans to go steerage under name William Jones (ticket). Wants "moral cowboy" life in West. Stranleigh offers grub-stake.
- Stranleigh bribes purser (£5 notes) to move Hazel to cabin 4390; Hazel keeps name John Hazel; promises no cards all the way across. Ponderby has 37 new suits; orders Hazel costumed.
- Girl (unnamed, "Miss Trevelyan", distant Wychwood-branch connection) lost purse (gold, notes, cabin ticket) on train from London. Stranleigh gives her two £50 notes (£100 loan), tells her to settle with purser; she was in cabin, cost £25.
- Night: Branksome Poole (burly, thick neck, "alleged husband") enters suite, claims wife received the two notes (numbers match). Stranleigh rejects blackmail; Poole names himself Branksome Poole, passenger list shows "Mr. and Mrs. Branksome Poole." Stranleigh has Ponderby throw him out; Poole's wife is in Ponderby's room.
- Wife's story: real name unnamed; father American-touring motorist, English chauffeur Charles Branksome (forged good family), married secretly in US, father refused to pay, died two years later, disinherited her. Branksome: liar, thief, forger, gambler, brute; wanted in NY for blackmailing millionaire Erasmus Blank. Stranleigh plans NY detention by wireless; advises divorce state; offers banking.
- Hazel plays poker with Poole; Poole deals; Hazel exposes cheating; chief officer, captain. Poole detained; wireless to NY police. Wife travels West unmolested with money incl. the two notes.

## Ch. II: An Automobile Ride
- Stranleigh in NY under Trevelyan; press hounds him; changes hotels with new names. Ponderby wants London.
- Wentworth Parkes: sent by letter from Duke of Rattleborough; pitches Sterling Motor Company, Detroit (J. E. Sterling, option); asks $100,000 stake. Stranleigh unimpressed.
- Motor ride; Stranleigh cables Rattleborough: letter forgery; Parkes was Rattleborough's valet 3 yrs, bolted with items, wanted by London police.
- Parkes sends aggrieved letters, threatens lawsuits.
- Stranleigh books steamer to Boston → St. John, New Brunswick, then Canada, then Detroit; under name Henry Johnson at hotel.
- Ponderby: Londoner, prefers Thames.
- Woodbridge Street shop: "J. E. STERLING. Motor Engineer." Young engineer Sterling (~25) with middle-aged assistant. Shows car with safety device: three pegs under leather curtain (centre stops engine/brakes; right turns right; left turns left). Stranleigh asks to borrow car. Sterling earlier gave option to a plausible Englishman (Parkes) who borrowed car 4 months ago.
- Stranleigh pays $500 for one-week option (5 × $100 bills); refuses payment for Sterling's time.
- Parkes (disguised lightly, as chauffeur) drives Stranleigh along Canadian shore toward Lake St. Clair; demands $100,000 at cliff edge. Stranleigh wrests wheel, uses pegs, stops car, throws Parkes into shallow river. Warns him re police/Rattleborough.
- Stranleigh has Sterling pay Parkes $500 (+$500 from Stranleigh) with legal promise not to molest; capitalisation $100,000–$500,000.

## Ch. III: The God in the Car
- Stranleigh as Henry Johnson, chauffeur; Ponderby as "Mr. Ponderby," country gentleman; Altonville (village in northern NY/Indian summer); Ponderby given $15,000 in Altonville bank (Burford/Lenthall butler precedent).
- Lakes, mills in decline. Young lovers; Mrs. Challis sprained ankle; husband James (Jim) Challis, ex-engineer, grist mill (Fulmer's) shut. Stranleigh drives them home; doctor (Altonville, unnamed) treats.
- Challis: engineer for Langdon, Bliss & Co.; assessed Stanmore Anson's factory (Anson's Mill). Anson fought the Trust (G.K.R. Trust); Langdon fired Anson-ordered; Challis married Anson's daughter Gertrude; Anson disinherited/refused to let her take belongings; Challis dismissed.
- Stranleigh buys Anson's Mill for Anson's stated sum; Anson demands manager be his choice; Challis named manager (Anson reconciles: "I did you a great injustice"). Gertrude: "Shall we throw our differences on that scrap-heap?" Stranleigh pays to clear auction posters; Anson's mansion also auctioned; Stranleigh uses Asa Perkins's summer house (Boston) pretext for wardrobe.

## Ch. IV: The Mad Miss Maturin
- Edward (Ned) Trenton, Pennsylvania coal/railway man, Stranleigh's host. Sister Mrs. Vanderveldt (Sis; husband ex-Minister to Italy, dreamy scholar). Constance Maturin: heiress, adjoins estate; father's company; John L. Boscombe controls; father's limited-liability company.
- Ned's lawsuit: conservation dam; he blew up dam; Maturin's dam at Powerville; forests, lakes, dams, power-houses, telephone cottages; model city on heights above Powerville.
- Stranleigh talks with Constance on drive; she asks for capital; he says he is "the capitalist"; buys stock; Boscombe warns ("stark mad"); Stranleigh says nothing.
- Festival: dam bursts; valley town destroyed; Boscombe: "This is murder!"; Stranleigh: "Whoever is responsible for the weakness of that dam should be hanged!"

## Ch. V: In Search of Game
- NY University Club; Banks (Ice Trust attorney) sends Stranleigh to Stanley Armstrong's ranch (letter; Bleachers station, Wyoming-ish West). Guide and escort desert after shot in left shoulder from Jim Dean (warning shot).
- Armstrong absent (in Chicago/walking). Daughter Miss Armstrong, doctor (Lausanne, professor), dresses wound; Thun trip; Jim Dean "shooting at sheriff."
- Father's debt to lawyer Silas A. Ricketts (Bleachers), $5,000 note, ranch security; silver mine; Ricketts sale; Stranleigh offers $2,000 + $3,000 loan; Ricketts refuses.

## Ch. VI: The Bunk House Prisoner
- Stranleigh inspects mine (dynamite stored); Jim Dean's warnings; invents line; Stranleigh goes to Bleachers, pays Ricketts $5 for time; telegraphs NY detective (Burns) and Pinkerton (Chicago) for Armstrong; orders $20,000 from NY agent.
- Telegraph operator bribed; Ricketts tracks. Stranleigh captured at dusk by six men; locked in bunk house.

## Ch. VII: The End of the Contest
- Stranleigh escapes via chimney, arms self with rifle, bread, ham, dynamite wall, shoots Jim's ear (letter "S" in door). Armistice. Miss Armstrong notices handkerchief with crest (Stranleigh's).
- Stranleigh hires six men as bodyguard ($50 each); meets Armstrong (Armstrong's $200 from Stranleigh; Armstrong's $500 bribe to sheriff). Auction in Agricultural Hall: Ricketts bids; Stranleigh wins at $17,000 cash.
- Stranleigh gives ranch deed to Miss Armstrong as "medical bill" (incl. Jim's); condition: keep in her name; Armstrong gets ~$10–12k. Stranleigh promises capital for mine. Miss Armstrong: "Lord Stranleigh of Wychwood." THE END.
